corrections: Dedicated MV-22B body sections, cockpit aperture, forward-swept wing, twin-fin tail, wing fairing, tapered fuel/gear sponsons and six wheels replace the generic shape. Exterior overlays corrected tail span, main-gear track, sponson width and an unclosed side-window patch. Nacelles have intake/exhaust details and independent three-blade proprotors.

Four main displays, offset standby instruments, upper autoflight/radio housings, lower central display, paired keypads, cyclics, two thrust levers with nacelle thumbwheels and distinct overhead lighting/APU/engine groups follow the photo/manual. Overhead was lowered to remove roof clipping.

Live TAS, geometric altitude, true heading, vertical speed, attitude, independent normalized engine RPM and nacelle-angle indicators use named variables. Gear, flaperons, elevators, rudders and controls animate; unsupported navigation and system readouts stay blank. The hover flaperon schedule is an explicit visual approximation.

Added actual imported-model checks for hover/transition/airplane axes, rotor rotation, trailing-edge motion, missing data and both model/Earth renderer paths. Corrected a nacelle-gauge/assembly name collision. Generator now carries exterior animation variable dependencies into the separate Earth animation evaluator.
reviewNotes.independentDimensions: Manufacturer17.47m fuselage,25.8m span and11.6m rotor diameter corroborate the manual. Model uses17.48m,25.78m and11.6m, with14.18m rotor-center spacing. Tail span corrected to5.54m from independent frontal/plan references. Nominal6.73m height excludes small hub details; geometry reaches6.79m. The side illustration draws a taller fin than the independent frontal height; model uses5.47m fin height. Cockpit width2.1m and cabin dimensions remain estimated.
reviewNotes.visual: Personally inspected all four final-hash overlays, eight standard views and15 close/state views: zero, cruise, limits, below-sea-level, missing readings, console, overhead, front detail, hover, half conversion, airplane configuration, tail, both control extremes and seats. Geometry/sightline validation,25 instrument tests including the MV-22 dual-renderer test, and byte-identical candidate regeneration passed.
limitations: General arrangements and the CC drawing are illustrative, with inconsistent side/front fin proportions and rotor phase. Cross-sections, airfoils, glazing, nacelle ducts and sponsons remain approximations rather than production station data. The exterior photo supports the frontal appearance, but is not a metrically calibrated view.

Cockpit dimensions are estimated. The photo has perspective, a helmet obscuring the autoflight unit, and a cropped right display. Main layout is reference-based; screen pages and labels are original simulator adaptations. Side panels, seats, belts, wiring and upholstery remain simplified. The overhead is lowered slightly for clearance within the reconstructed roof.

Speed is TAS, altitude geometric, heading true, RPM normalized simulator shaft speed and nozzle angle0–90degrees. These are not certified V-22 avionics. Electrical power, fuel, temperature, torque, navigation, radio, warning systems and autopilot are unsupported and do not show invented readings. The engine model does not simulate the real interconnecting drive shaft.

Gear uses translation/hiding without full linkage sequencing. Conversion is0–90degrees; aft-of-vertical nacelle travel, blade folding, wing stow, flapping/coning and cargo-ramp motion are not implemented. Hover flaperon scheduling is a visual approximation. The cargo cabin is unfurnished. Selective seams/fasteners are not a manufacturing rivet schedule. Assisted flight checks do not establish real aircraft performance.

The deck height is inferred from the eye, not measured. The outer PFD horizon mask in the shared instrument-geometry helper extends about 0.09 m past the side glass at its top corner; it does not show from the front or the nose view. Wipers set the sweep overNose reading at -5 degrees.

cockpitReview.method: Rays from the pilotEye through source.glb (cockpit-sweep), seat view at the runtime camera (+Z, 60 degrees vertical), an exterior nose render, and sections through the pilot plane and at hood height, each checked against a photograph of the real aircraft.
findings: The seat stood 0.35 m aft of the eye, which was ahead of the cushion: the ray down reached the floor at 1.58 m and the seatback lay 0.55 m behind the shoulders.
The eye, hood and glass agree, and the eye stood 1.13 m over the cushion, so the seat was too low. The crew need a raised deck: the floor continued level from the cabin.
A glareshield shelf and two radio boxes reached past the side glass: the 0.2 percent poked reading.
corrections: Crew deck raised 0.32 m under the seats and pedals. Seats slid 0.25 m forward and raised 0.33 m.
Sticks, thrust levers, pedals, sideboards and console follow; eye and panel unchanged.
Glareshield shelf and radio boxes trimmed inside the glass.
